title: The model version that actually served a response is never recorded, so a provider-side behaviour change cannot be attributed or pinned
problem: My agent got worse this week and I cannot tell whether my prompt change did it or the provider moved the model under me, because nothing in my logs says which model version answered.
symptom: The call site names a floating alias or an environment variable, the response object carries a resolved model identifier that the application throws away, and a regression investigation has no way to separate a change made in the repository from a change made upstream.
why_now: Providers ship behaviour changes continuously and expose the resolved version on every response, so the data needed to attribute a regression is already in hand at runtime and is routinely discarded; the missing piece is a convention that records it, not a new API.
existing: Alias-to-snapshot pinning removes the drift but only if a project actually pins, and pinning alone still records nothing, so an investigation cannot prove which version ran for a past request.
Provider status pages and deprecation notices announce planned retirements, not the behavioural deltas of a routine update, and they are not correlated with a given customer request.

evidence.title: A postmortem of three recent issues
evidence.quote: Although we were aware of an increase in reports online, we lacked a clear way to connect these to each of our recent changes.
evidence.note: The vendor with the most instrumentation still could not attribute a behaviour change to the deploy that caused it; a consumer who records no served version has strictly less to work with.

evidence.title: Expanding on what we missed with sycophancy
evidence.quote: Even with what we thought were all the right ingredients in place (A/B tests, offline evals, expert reviews), we still missed this important issue.
evidence.note: Model updates do change behaviour in ways pre-launch review misses, which is exactly the class of change a consumer can only detect after the fact and only if the served version was recorded.

build_hypothesis: A thin client wrapper that refuses a floating alias unless an explicit opt-in flag is set, and writes the resolved model identifier returned on the response into the same log line as the request id.

check.manual_question: For a response your system produced last week, can you name the exact model version that generated it, and would a provider-side version change be visible to you without a customer telling you?
check.rationale: A floating alias or an environment-supplied model id means the served version is chosen outside the repository, and the absence of any served-model or model-version token means the resolved identifier the provider returns is never persisted, so a behaviour change has no attributable cause. It can be wrong where the version is recorded by a logging sidecar or a gateway outside this repository, which is what the manual question is for.

bad.app/llm.py:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4-5-latest"

def answer(question: str) -> str:
    reply = client.messages.create(
        model=MODEL,
        max_tokens=512,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}],
    )
    return reply.content[0].text

good.app/llm.py:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# Pinned snapshot: the served version cannot change without a code change,
# and the version that actually answered is logged with every call so a
# regression can be attributed to a deploy rather than guessed at.
MODEL_SNAPSHOT = "claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929"

def answer(question: str) -> str:
    reply = client.messages.create(
        model=MODEL_SNAPSHOT,
        max_tokens=512,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}],
    )
    log_call(requested=MODEL_SNAPSHOT, served_model=reply.model)
    return reply.content[0].text
